warnings: This paper focuses on nutrient CYCLING and UPTAKE rather than just concentrations - many tables show fluxes and pools rather than tissue concentrations
Treatment/control terminology uses 'ambient' vs 'elevated' - ambient is control
Unbalanced design: 2 elevated CO2 plots vs 3 ambient plots due to experimental issues
Some soil chemical properties showed pre-treatment differences between plots
Wood nutrient concentrations were measured outside treatment plots and assumed equal across treatments
Multiple measurement methods used for some nutrients (water collectors vs resin collectors)
WARNING: SCANNED PDF - Text may have OCR errors
WARNING: VAR-UNCLEAR - Variance type not clearly stated
recon.variance_source: ampling areas was used to calculate the mean and standard error for both the ambient and the elevated CO2\n
recon.treatment_definition: Elevated CO2 (average daytime [CO2] of 542 ppm during 1999-2000 growing seasons)
recon.potential_tc_confusion: None - labeling is clear and consistent
recon.sample_size_source: two plots instrumented with FACE apparatus... This gave two replicates for elevated and three for ambient
recon.extraction_guidance: Focus on Table 4 for tissue mineral concentrations in foliage, litterfall, and fine roots. This is the primary table with target outcome variables. Table 2 contains some nutrient data but mainly ecosystem pools/contents rather than concentrations. Ignore Tables 1, 3, 5-7 as they contain soil properties, fluxes, ratios, and soil solution data rather than plant tissue concentrations. Very small sample sizes (n=2-3) may limit statistical power.

table_descriptions.Table 1: Pre-treatment soil chemical and physical properties by depth
table_descriptions.Table 2: Ecosystem contents of C, N, P, K, Ca, Mg in vegetation, forest floor, and soil
table_descriptions.Table 3: Nutrient fluxes including atmospheric deposition, throughfall, litterfall, root turnover, wood increment, and uptake
table_descriptions.Table 4: Nutrient concentrations in foliage, litterfall, and fine roots
table_descriptions.Table 5: Carbon production per unit nutrient uptake and requirement ratios
table_descriptions.Table 6: Soil solution concentrations and statistical analyses

recon.extraction_method_reason: Scanned/image tables - use vision to supplement text
challenge_hints: Verify all numbers carefully - OCR may confuse 0/O, 1/l/I
If numbers look wrong, flag for manual review
Check Methods section for 'mean ± SE' or 'mean ± SD' statement
Check table footnotes for variance definitions
